[Task index](core.md) · [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md) · [Input](input.md)

HeadlessGameRunner(Game) runs the same portable callbacks with a device-free
Canvas, logical Audio, text control and an empty private save store. Its init
returns an allocated pointer; call runner.deinit once, and do not separately
destroy its Game, context capabilities or Canvas.

In runner signatures, `Self` means `up.testSupport.HeadlessGameRunner(Game)`.
`Input.Snapshot` is `up.input.Input.Snapshot`; `input_replay.Replay` is
`up.preview.developer.InputReplay`; `render.Command` is
`up.graphics.RenderCommand`. The recorder's source-local `Recorder` and
`Replay` use the public preview aliases listed below.

## Record and reproduce a small run

This executed function uses the [portable Game](lifecycle.md), records a fixed
tick with a committed Unicode string, encodes/parses UPR5, and asserts state
after replay. Recorder owns its buffers; finish returns a separately owned
Replay, encode returns owned bytes, and parsing returns another owned Replay.
Each uses the same allocator for release.

[Compiled source](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig#L74) (`replay`):

```zig
pub fn replay(allocator: std.mem.Allocator) !u64 {
    var recorder = try up.preview.developer.InputReplayRecorder.initSeeded(allocator, 60, 42);
    defer recorder.deinit();
    var input = up.input.Input{};
    input.set(.right, true);
    input.setTextInputActive(true); // Test the observation after host activation.
    try input.commitText("Zoë");
    try recorder.record(input);
    var recorded = try recorder.finish();
    defer recorded.deinit(allocator);
    const bytes = try recorded.encode(allocator);
    defer allocator.free(bytes);
    var decoded = try up.preview.developer.parseInputReplay(allocator, bytes);
    defer decoded.deinit(allocator);
    const runner = try up.testSupport.HeadlessGameRunner(Game).initSeeded(allocator, 64, 24, 42);
    defer runner.deinit();
    try runner.runReplay(decoded);
    if (runner.game.x != 41 or !std.mem.eql(u8, runner.game.name[0..runner.game.name_len], "Zoë")) return error.ReplayStateMismatch;
    return runner.capture().image_hash; // Capture borrows the runner.
}
```


The example returns a capture hash before destroying the runner. Captured
commands and CanvasTrace borrow runner storage until its next draw or deinit.
Do not store their pointers as a permanent snapshot.

## Boundaries, errors and reproducibility

step advances one update without drawing; draw does not advance simulation.
runReplay validates input before execution. initSeeded supplies the selected
seed during Game.init. Equal input alone is insufficient if initialization
uses different saves, wall-clock time or uncontrolled randomness.

For save-dependent bugs, use recorder.initSession **before Game.init**, select
the required save keys and identity, then use runner.initReplay on a fresh
runner. It restores those captured saves into private storage without writing
user data. Identity/seed/environment errors include
`ReplayIdentityRequired`, `ReplayGameMismatch`, `ReplayBuildMismatch`,
`ReplayAssetsMismatch`, `ReplaySeedMismatch`, `ReplayEnvironmentRequired`
and `ReplayAlreadyStarted`. Invalid snapshots/time/alpha are rejected.
The [full testing guide](../guides/testing.md) explains formats, bounds, errors,
logical trace comparisons and existing pixel/replay goldens.

Replay record/parse lives under **preview.developer** and remains optional
developer tooling. This reference does not promote its stability or browser
renderer status. The headless APIs do not require SDL or a GPU.

Use StateHash.updatePortable on chosen fixed-width game fields to avoid
native struct padding and target-sized integers; use updateBytes for strings.
The legacy updateValue uses native representation and retains its old hashes.
InMemorySaveStore owns copied values and must stay at a stable address after
init because its capability points back to it; a runner borrowing that store
must be destroyed first.

<a id="testSupport-StateHash-updatePortable"></a>
### `up.testSupport.StateHash.updatePortable`

[Source declaration](../../src/test_support.zig#L399).

Hashes logical fields without Zig padding, pointers, or native byte
order. Use fixed-width game fields (u32 rather than usize), and keep
their order/types stable. Floats use exact IEEE bits, including -0.
Slices and pointers are deliberately excluded; use updateBytes for a
byte string or iterate the game-owned elements explicitly.

```zig
pub fn updatePortable(self: *StateHash, value: anytype) void;
```

[Source declaration](../../src/test_support.zig#L427).

<a id="preview-developer-InputReplay-encode"></a>
### `up.preview.developer.InputReplay.encode`

[Source declaration](../../src/input_replay.zig#L71).

Produces fixed-width, little-endian replay data. Seedless replays emit
UPR2; seed-bearing replays emit UPR3 with an explicit algorithm ID and
seed. Session recordings emit UPR4 with initial saves and identity.
Physical/text extension data selects UPR5 with optional seed/session
metadata and length-delimited extensions. All earlier formats remain
readable through `parse`; normalized-only output is unchanged.

```zig
pub fn encode(self: Replay, allocator: std.mem.Allocator) ![]u8;
```

## `up.preview.developer.parseInputReplay`

[Source declaration](../../src/input_replay.zig#L163). Implementation name: `parse`.

Parses UPR4 session data, UPR3 seed-bearing data, UPR2 seedless data, or older
UPR1 run-length text fixtures. UPR1 carries only held action keys; its
edges are reconstructed from successive held states.
